newsitem.title: USA: Colo. Comanche coal-fired unit restart delayed.
newsitem.headline: Colo. Comanche coal-fired unit restart delayed.

text.p: The 350 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Comanche coal-fired power plant in Pueblo, Colo., is tentatively expected to be back on line January 29, a spokeswoman for Public Service Co Colorado said Monday.
Repairs to the unit, which has been out of service since a fire in a cable tray on December 18, are expected to be finished this week, she added.
PS Colorado said early this month the unit would be back on line by today, but the repair work is still underway.
"The operators are not sure how long start-up will take, but we are anticipating January 29," the spokeswoman noted.
Comanche's 350 MW unit 2 was said to be operating normally.
PS Colorado is owner and operator of the Comanche plant.
